title: Model intake: scenarios, acceptance runbook, and owner rota (v0.1)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working runbook for intake of new open / community models into the Redwood inference stack. Focus is on scenario-driven evaluation (what we actually care about in production), clear go/no-go thresholds, and a lightweight owner rota so every intake has a named responsible party for follow-up and remediation.

Scope:
- Applies to new model versions or community models proposed for Hosted API, Dedicated pools, or Private deployment.
- Intended to be used by applied-ml owners running the initial fast-eval (2–3 days) and the full regression suite (1–2 weeks).
- NOT a prescriptive training checklist; this is an inference/eval intake document.

High-level flow (timeboxed):
1) Intake triage (day 0): owner assigns, quick docs check, dataset links validated, license/compatibility check. (30–60m)
2) Smoke run (day 0–1): run 20 representative prompts across 5 scenarios to catch obvious breakage and latency issues. (2–4h)
3) Scenario sweep (day 1–3): run full scenario matrix (below) with automated metrics + spot human review.
4) Regression run (day 3–7): compare to baseline model(s) using numeric thresholds; escalate if regressions exceed limits.
5) Decision & next steps (day 7): accept / accept-with-conditions / reject. If accepted, owner files onboarding ticket for serving team and sets up monitoring.

Roles and owner rota:
- Intake owner (primary): responsible for running the runs, filing tickets, communicating results. Rota: weekly rotation across appliied-ml triage team. 
- Baseline owner (secondary): picks baseline model(s) for comparison and confirms evaluation queries.
- Security reviewer: quick check for obviously unsafe content or licensing red flags.
- Ops contact: for any infra/latency/SGVM issues.

Example owner rota (quarterly snapshot):
- Week 1: Asha Gonzalez (primary) / Marcus Li (baseline)
- Week 2: Samira Khan / Jonah Reeves
- Week 3: Jonah Reeves / Evan Park
- Week 4: Marcus Li / Asha Gonzalez
(rotate and adjust based on capacity)

Decision matrix (simple):
- Accept: no major regressions, latency within SLO, non-problematic safety/toxicity signals, license ok.
- Accept with conditions: minor regressions in non-critical scenarios OR requires quantized build tuning before production; require follow-up checklist and re-run window.
- Reject: major regressions on production-critical scenarios, unresolvable safety or license issues.

Scenario matrix (must-run):
1) Instruction-following (IF): 200 prompts, mix of short/long instructions, evaluate instruction pass rate (binary rubric: correct/incorrect). Target: >= 92% pass rate vs baseline.
2) Dialog coherence (DC): 100 multi-turn threads (3–6 turns), evaluate coherence drift and hallucination. Metric: human score median >= baseline - 0.25 (0–5 scale).
3) Code synthesis (CS): 100 coding prompts (python, SQL), measure functional correctness via unit tests where available. Target: functional pass >= baseline - 5pp.
4) Retrieval-augmented QA (RAG): 150 prompts using our internal retrieval pipeline; measure F1/token-overlap and hallucination count. Target: no >10% drop in F1 for high-recall queries.
5) Safety/toxicity (ST): 500 adversarial probes + existing safety suite. Block if toxicity-likelihood > 0.8 or more than 2 high-severity hits.
6) Latency & throughput (L/T): standardized perf harness with sequence length distribution sampled from production: P95 latency <= 1.25x baseline P95; throughput within 80% of capacity on Dedicated pools.
7) Cost profile (COST): estimate token cost delta and CPU/GPU time per request. Accept only if projected unit cost <= 1.2x baseline unless explicit business case.

Evaluation artifacts and where to run them:
- Eval harness repo: github.com/redwood-inference/model-eval-playbook (use the intake branch + provided runner).
- Datasets: gs://redwood-eval-buckets/intake-datasets/{scenario}/
- Local testbed: small smoke infra (k8s-dev), if perf tests needed use perf cluster tag: perf-intake-1.

Prompt set notes (quick starters):
- IF prompts: mix of instruction types (summarize, transform, reason, explain), include edge-case negations, long context (1k tokens), two-shot examples.
- DC threads: seed with user utterances taken from anonymized production logs (where allowed) + synthetic roles.
- CS prompts: include function spec, unit test scaffolding; prefer short to medium code blocks for fast test runs.
- RAG: sample from support docs + contrived adversarial queries.
- Safety probes: use existing safety-suite + proprietary adversarial set (see linked artifact).

Acceptance thresholds (example table as prose):
- IF pass rate: must be >= 92% absolute OR within 1.5pp of baseline if baseline pass rate < 92%.
- DC median human score: no more than 0.25 drop from baseline median.
- CS functional pass: no more than 5 percentage points below baseline.
- RAG F1: no more than 10% relative drop on high-recall queries.
- Safety: zero high-severity fails, + investigations for any new medium-severity hits.
- Latency: P95 <= 1.25x baseline; P99 requires explicit ops signoff.
- Cost: unit cost <= 1.2x baseline without product signoff.

Quick smoke script (to run immediately on intake):
- Checkout intake branch of eval harness.
- Load 20 quick prompts (one file: smoke_if.txt, smoke_dc.json for threads).
- Run: python run_smoke.py --model <candidate> --prompts smoke_set/
- Capture: sample outputs, P95 latency, error traces, and 5 spot human review items.
- If smoke fails any hard block (e.g., crash, timeouts, immediate safety flag), escalate to ops and security.

Regression reporting format (deliverable):
- Single JSON summary (already generated by harness) + 1-page human summary with top 5 regressions or improvements, example failing prompts, and recommended action.
- Fields we expect in the summary (string list for the report): run_id, model_name, baseline_name, scenario, metric, baseline_value, candidate_value, delta, severity_flag, blocking_reason (if any), owner_action.
- Attach 10 representative failing prompts with model outputs and baseline outputs.

Go-to-production checklist (if accepted):
- Create onboarding ticket in the Serving backlog (tag: onboarding, model:<name>)
- Pin quantization/profile if used; attach quantized artifact to ticket.
- Create monitoring dashboard: quality probes (monthly), cost telemetry, lat/err traces.
- Add hard-coded fallback policy: fallback to baseline model if safety trigger or P95 latency > 2x.
- Define canary rollout policy: start 1% for 48h, 5% 72h, then evaluate.

Open questions & TODOs (working list):
- Do we need a separate acceptance threshold for hallucination (explicit metric) or leverage DC/RAG deltas? (TODO: propose metric by next week)
- Small-model vs quantized model acceptance: how to standardize cost vs quality tradeoffs? (TODO: propose profiling template)
- Owner rota automation: create a simple calendar with weekly assignment (JIRA automation) (TODO: Marcus).

Notes to reviewer:
- This is a lightweight, scenario-first runbook intended to speed up intake while preventing major regressions from reaching production. Expect edits: we should add links to specific harness run command examples and a sample regression JSON template in the repo.
- If you take ownership of a week, please update the rota table above and add yourself to the collaborators list.

Appendix (quick links and commands):
- Eval harness: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-eval-playbook && cd model-eval-playbook && git checkout intake-runner
- Smoke run example: python runners/smoke_run.py --model <candidate> --prompts smoke_sets/if_short.txt --out results/<model>-smoke.json- Compare: python tools/compare_to_baseline.py --candidate results/<model>-smoke.json --baseline results/<baseline>-smoke.json

End of draft.
